'''Howard E. Zimmerman''' (July 5, 1926 – February 12, 2012) was a professor of chemistry at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]].<ref>{{Cite web
| title = Faculty Info
| publisher = University of Wisconsin
| access-date = 2010-04-05
| url = http://www.chem.wisc.edu/content/faculty-info#Z
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120818225246/http://www.chem.wisc.edu/content/faculty-info#Z
| archive-date = 2012-08-18
| url-status = dead
}}</ref> He was elected to the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] in 1980<ref>{{Cite web
| title = National Academy of Sciences
| access-date = 2010-04-05
| url = http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir/701333752?pg=rslts
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110622064625/http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir/701333752?pg=rslts
| archive-date = 2011-06-22
| url-status = dead
}}</ref> and the recipient of the 1986 [[American Institute of Chemists]] [[Chemical Pioneer Award]].<ref>{{Cite web
| title = Chemical Pioneer Award
|publisher=American Institute of Chemists
| access-date = 2010-04-05
| url = http://www.theaic.org/desktopdefault.aspx?tabid=57
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20040117124742/http://www.theaic.org/DesktopDefault.aspx?tabid=57
| archive-date = 2004-01-17
}}</ref><ref>Schuster, D. I. (2012), Howard E. Zimmerman (1926–2012). Angew. Chem. Int. Ed., 51: 5286–5288. {{doi|10.1002/anie.201202970}}</ref>

==Biography==
Howard E. Zimmerman was a native of [[Connecticut]].<ref>{{Cite web
| title = EPA Newsletter
| publisher = European Phocochemistry Association
| date = December 2006
| access-date = 2010-04-07
| url = http://www.photochemistry.eu/newsletter/EPA_NEWSLETTER_dec_2006.pdf
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110720171220/http://www.photochemistry.eu/newsletter/EPA_NEWSLETTER_dec_2006.pdf
| archive-date = 2011-07-20
| url-status = live
}}</ref> During [[World War II]], he served in the [[I Armored Corps (United States)|U.S. Armored Corps]] in Europe where he was a tank gunner. His final rank was [[technical sergeant]].<ref name=iaps/> He obtained a B. S. in Chemistry in 1950 and a Ph.D. in 1953 both from [[Yale University]].<ref name=iaps/> He was a Postdoctoral Research Fellow with a [[United States National Research Council|National Research Council]] fellowship from 1953 to 1954 working with [[R. B. Woodward]] (Harvard).<ref name=iaps/> From 1954 to 1960 he was assistant professor at [[Northwestern University]].<ref name=iaps/> Beginning in 1960 he was Associate Professor and then Professor at the [[University of Wisconsin]],<ref name=iaps/> and from 1990 he was Hilldale and A. C. Cope Professor of Chemistry. His publications number over 285 (including 11 chapters).

Zimmerman gave ACS Short Courses on organic [[quantum chemistry]] and [[molecular orbital theory]]. He authored a 1975 textbook entitled ''Quantum Mechanics for Organic Chemists''.<ref>{{cite book|last=Zimmerman|first=Howard E.|title=Quantum mechanics for organic chemists|publisher=Academic Press|location=New York|year=1975|isbn=978-0-12-781650-0|oclc=1104091|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/quantummechanics00zimm}}</ref> Zimmerman was the organizer of the 1972 [[IUPAC]] [[Photochemistry]] Symposium ([[Baden-Baden]]) and of five [[Pacifichem]] Symposia – the last being Pacifichem 2010.
